analysis.one_liner: Creates an ACA insurance marketplace and extends premium tax credits to Puerto Rico residents.
analysis.headline: A bill to give Puerto Rico residents access to ACA premium tax credits, introduced December 4, 2025, has been referred to two House committees and has not moved since.
analysis.plain_summary: This bill would require the federal government to set up an Affordable Care Act insurance marketplace in Puerto Rico, apply the ACA's health insurance rules there, and let island residents claim the same premium tax credits that residents of the 50 states can claim. Today, Puerto Rico is treated differently under the ACA, and its residents cannot get these subsidies. The bill has one sponsor and one cosponsor, both House Democrats from Florida, and has not received a hearing or a vote.
analysis.who_benefits: Puerto Rico's roughly 3 million residents, especially people who buy their own health insurance and currently cannot receive federal premium tax credits because the territory is excluded from the ACA's tax-credit rules.
analysis.who_benefits_short: Puerto Rico residents buying their own insurance

how_it_helps.text: The bill amends the ACA to require an Exchange (the insurance marketplace) to be established in Puerto Rico within one year of enactment.
It overrides a 2014 federal decision and applies the ACA's health insurance market reforms, such as protections for people with pre-existing conditions, to health coverage sold in Puerto Rico.
It amends the federal tax code so that for premium tax credit purposes, Puerto Rico is treated the same as a state, letting island residents claim subsidies that residents of the 50 states can claim.

analysis.who_pays: The federal treasury, which would bear the cost of the new premium tax credits for Puerto Rico residents; private insurers in Puerto Rico would also face new ACA market rules.
analysis.who_pays_short: Federal taxpayers; Puerto Rico insurers face new rules

drawbacks.text: The bill has no cost estimate in the record; extending premium tax credits to Puerto Rico would add federal spending, and the bill text includes no offsetting pay-for.

The premium tax credit is tied to income relative to the federal poverty line, and poverty in Puerto Rico is much higher than on the mainland; many of the island's lowest-income residents would earn too little to benefit from these credits, a gap usually filled by Medicaid instead of by this bill.

With only one sponsor and one cosponsor, the bill would need far more support in both the House and Senate to become law, and no action has been taken since it was referred to two committees on December 4, 2025.

analysis.benefit_vs_cost: The core change is real and straightforward: it closes a gap in the ACA under which U.S. citizens living in Puerto Rico cannot claim the same health insurance subsidies as citizens in the states. The cost is federal spending with no offset, and the design has a known weakness, since tax credits help middle-income households more than the island's many very poor residents. On balance, for the people it reaches, the benefit is substantial.

outcome.mechanism: The bill was introduced on December 4, 2025 and sent to the Energy and Commerce and Ways and Means committees, where it has sat without a hearing or vote while the Congress continues.

narrative.text: Rep. Darren Soto introduced the bill on December 4, 2025, joined by one cosponsor.
The same day, it was referred to the House Energy and Commerce Committee and the House Ways and Means Committee, the two panels with authority over health coverage and the tax code.
No further action, hearing, markup, or vote has occurred.

outcome.who_came_out_ahead: So far, nothing has changed; Puerto Rico residents remain without ACA premium tax credits, and the bill's fate rests with committee chairs who have not scheduled any action.

analysis.who_came_out_ahead_short: No one yet; the bill is waiting

for.name: Rep. Darren Soto
for.role: Sponsor, House Energy and Commerce Committee member
for.what_they_did: Introduced the bill to extend the ACA marketplace, market reforms, and premium tax credits to Puerto Rico.

sides.party_line_note: Both sponsors are House Democrats, and no member of either party has opposed or supported the bill beyond the two sponsors; no committee or floor action has tested its support.

industries.industry: Health insurers selling coverage in Puerto Rico
industries.note: The bill would subject Puerto Rico insurers to ACA market rules, including pre-existing condition protections, while also creating a subsidized marketplace that channels federal tax credits through them as new customers. Insurers' interest in the new subsidized demand runs alongside residents' interest in affordable coverage.
Extending premium tax credits to Puerto Rico residents would add federal spending with no offset in the bill; taxpayers fund it, and Puerto Rico residents receive the benefit.

analysis.trajectory: With two sponsors, no hearing, and dual committee referral, the bill is unlikely to advance in the 119th Congress unless it gains substantially more cosponsors or is folded into a broader health or territories package; most territory-specific health bills at this stage die in committee.
